answer: Each identity provisions a lagoon voyage with one water cask and locks a 70-credit bond. The cask is filled at the lagoon and closed with a spiral seal whose serial is bound to the identity key and voyage date. Auditors check weight, salinity, and seal serial at departure; a reused serial or wrong salinity burns the bond. The first cask costs 33, the kth 33+6(k-1); 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 and pay 3,030,000, with no bulk discount. A rented-cask ring fails because one cask cannot file two key-bound fills in one voyage. An honest agent pays 33 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
